To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Robo1 and 2 have divergent functions in commissures because of differences in their protein structure and expression patterns, and that differences in expression patterns, not protein structure, are responsible for the differences in longitudinal axon guidance between the three Robo proteins.
the three Drosophila robo receptors (Robo1, Robob and Robo3) are expressed in different combinations in different axon pathways.
Robo1 and 2 are functionally distinct and their distinct functions rely on differences in their protein structures and their expression patterns.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control the formation of neuronal connections in the brain.
the development and evolution of the nervous system, and in particular with the mechanisms that control the formation of neural circuits.
the molecular basis of axon guidance, the process by which neurons navigate through the developing nervous system to establish connections with their targets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
The orthogonal array of axonal pathways in the D. melanogaster CNS is constructed in large part under the control the three Robo family receptors: Robo, Robo2, and Robo3."
Robo1 is required to inhibit crossing of longitudinal axons, Robo2 is required for the formation of commissures, and Robo3 is required for the guidance of axons in the ventral nerve cord.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Robo receptors are not interchangeable, and the functional diversity of Robo proteins is achieved by a combination of differential gene regulation and differences in protein structure.
Robo1 and 2 are not functionally redundant in Drosophila and that the distinct functions are due to distinct expression patterns and protein domains.
the Robos are not only differentially expressed, but also that they have different functional properties, which can be attributed to the differences in their protein domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same receptor can have different functions depending on where it is expressed.
the three Robo proteins in Drosophila can be functionally interchangeable.
distinct axon guidance functions can be conferred by differences in expression pattern and/or differences in protein structure.
